approved: Export Inspection (Establishment Registration Charges) Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would align definitions in several export inspection Acts to fix technical defects and allow the Department of Agriculture to recover costs for export services.
The bill would amend the Export Inspection (Establishment Registration Charges) Act 1985 to match its definitions with those in the Export Control Act 1982.
The explanatory memorandum says the changes are minor and technical in nature, and the bill would commence on the day it receives Royal Assent.
Align definitions in the Export Inspection (Establishment Registration Charges) Act 1985 with the Export Control Act 1982.
Enable the Department of Agriculture to recover costs for export services.
Remedy technical defects in the Export Control Act 1982 and related Acts.
The Department of Agriculture and businesses that pay establishment registration charges for export services.

Introduced the final of four export legislation bills, allowing the department to recover establishment registration charges from exporters of products like cut flowers, dried fruit, nursery stock, nuts, seed, timber and tissue culture without imposing new fees.

Summed up the debate on the Export Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 package, said Australia's farm, fish and forest exports were worth more than $41 billion in 2012 to 2013, and noted the Griffith area of his Riverina electorate generates about $800 million a year in wine exports from three-quarters of New South Wales' wine grapes.
